The test image shows a soybean stem near the soil line with reddish-brown to dark chocolate-brown discoloration extending upward from the soil level, with darker spots visible. Key candidates:
- **Phytophthora**: dark chocolate-brown lower stem discoloration extending upward from soil line
- **Rhizoctonia**: reddish-brown lesions at soil line
- **Fusarium**: reddish-brown root/stem discoloration

The test image shows a close-up of a soybean lower stem near the soil line with prominent reddish-brown to dark brown discoloration. This is the classic diagnostic view for Phytophthora — the dark chocolate-brown stem lesion extending from soil level upward. The Phytophthora reference image confirms the associated wilting/dead leaves remaining attached.

The discoloration pattern in the test image (reddish-brown extending up the stem at soil level) matches Phytophthora's key diagnostic feature perfectly: "dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from below the soil line upward several nodes."
